questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a maximization integer program with incumbent value $L$, a node's LP relaxation has optimal value $U$. Which situation is NOT a reason to prune the node?
options: Its LP relaxation has no feasible point.
Its LP optimum is fractional and $U>L$.
Its LP optimum satisfies all integer restrictions.
Its LP value satisfies $U\le L$.

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a maximization integer program, $L$ is the incumbent value and $U$ the LP relaxation value of a node. Which comparison allows the node to be pruned by its bound?
options: $U\ge L$
$U=L$ only
$U\le L$

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a minimization integer program with incumbent cost $L$, a node's LP relaxation has optimal value $z_R$. When can the node be pruned by its bound?
options: When $z_R\le L$
When $z_R>2L$
When $z_R\ge L$
When $z_R$ is integral

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a maximization integer program, a node's LP relaxation optimum is integral with value larger than the incumbent value $L$. What is done with this node?
options: It becomes the incumbent, and the node is pruned.
It is pruned, and the incumbent value $L$ is kept.
It becomes the incumbent, and the node is branched.
It is branched, since only leaf nodes are pruned.

questions.question: Branch-and-bound prunes nodes that are infeasible, integral, or bounded by the incumbent. What do these three pruning conditions have in common?
options: Each shows that the node's LP optimum is the global optimum.
Each removes nodes likely, but not certain, to be useless.
Each proves that subdividing it cannot beat the incumbent.
Each applies only once the incumbent has been proven optimal.

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a maximization integer program, the incumbent value is 27. A node's LP relaxation gives a fractional optimum with value 26.5. What happens to the node?
options: It is branched, since it is fractional.
It is pruned, since $26.5\le27$ holds.
It is kept, since $26.5$ rounds to 27.
It becomes the incumbent with 26.5.

questions.question: An integer program has the constraint $2x_1+4x_3\le18$ with $x_1,x_3\ge0$. In branch-and-bound a node is created by adding the branch $x_3\ge5$. Why can this node be pruned?
options: Its LP is infeasible: $4x_3\ge20>18$.
Its LP value is below the incumbent.
Its LP optimum is integral at $x_3=5$.
It repeats its parent, so it is redundant.

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a maximization integer program the incumbent value is 30. A node's LP relaxation optimum is integral with value 33. What are the incumbent value and the node's status afterwards?
options: Incumbent 30; the node is pruned.
Incumbent 33; the node is branched.
Incumbent 30; the node is branched.
Incumbent 33; the node is pruned.

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a minimization integer program the incumbent cost is 120. Three open nodes have fractional LP optima with values 118.5, 120 and 125. Which of them can be pruned by bound?
options: Only the node with value 125
Only the node with value 118.5
The nodes with values 120 and 125
None, since all three are fractional

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a maximization integer program the incumbent value is 40, and the active unresolved nodes have LP bounds 43.5, 41 and 39. What is the valid global upper bound on the optimal value?
options: 43.5, the largest open bound
40, the incumbent value
41, the bound just above 40
39, the smallest open-node bound

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a maximization integer program, nodes are pruned when $U\le L$, including the case $U=L$, where $U$ is a node's LP value and $L$ the incumbent value. A planner wants a list of ALL optimal solutions. What does the equality case cost?
options: It can discard other equally optimal solutions.
It can give a wrong optimal value at the end.
It can make the incumbent an infeasible point.
Nothing, since a node with $U=L$ has no solution.

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a maximization integer program, a node was pruned when the incumbent value was 20 because its LP bound was 19. Later the incumbent improves to 24. Must the pruned node be reopened?
options: Yes: a better incumbent changes every node's bound.
No: its bound 19 also lies below the new value 24.
Yes: all pruned nodes are rechecked at each update.
No: pruned nodes contain no integer points at all.

questions.question: Branch-and-bound is applied to a maximization program with three binary variables $x_1,x_2,x_3$. The node $x_1=0$ is pruned by bound at depth one. How many of the 8 complete 0/1 assignments are thereby excluded without being evaluated?
options: 1, the node's LP solution at $x_1=0$
4, all the assignments that have $x_1=0$
2, one per remaining variable $x_2$, $x_3$
0, as each assignment is still checked later

questions.question: For: maximize $3x_1+2x_2$ subject to $2x_1+2x_2\le9.5$, $x_1\le3.5$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$ integer, branch-and-bound has incumbent $(3,1)$ with value 11. The node with $x_2\ge2$, $x_1\le2$, $x_2\le2$ has LP optimum $(2,2)$ with value 10. What happens?
options: $(2,2)$ becomes incumbent and the node is pruned.
It is branched, since $x_2\le2$ is still active.
It stays open until all other nodes are solved.
It is pruned, and the incumbent stays at $(3,1)$.

questions.question: For: maximize $3x_1+2x_2$ subject to $2x_1+2x_2\le9.5$, $x_1\le3.5$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$ integer, branch-and-bound reaches the node with branch constraints $x_2\ge3$ and $x_1\ge2$. What happens to this node?
options: It is pruned: its bound is below the incumbent.
It gets the integral optimum $(2,3)$, value 12.
It is pruned as infeasible: $2\cdot2+2\cdot3=10>9.5$.
It is branched on $x_1$, as $x_1\le3.5$ allows more.

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a maximization integer program the incumbent value improves from 18 to 20. The open nodes have fractional LP optima with bounds 19.5, 20 and $62/3\approx20.67$. Which of them still need branching?
options: All three, as they were open before
The nodes with bounds 20 and $62/3$
None, as the incumbent improved
Only the node with bound $62/3$

questions.question: When branch-and-bound for a maximization integer program finishes, every node has been branched or pruned. Why does this prove that the final incumbent is optimal?
options: Its value equals the root LP value at the very end.
It was the last integral solution to be found.
All integer points were evaluated one by one.
Every region was searched or proved unable to win.

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a maximization integer program with incumbent value 30, a student cannot solve a node's LP exactly and instead finds a feasible point of that LP with value 28. The student prunes the node because $28\le30$. What is wrong?
options: 28 is no bound: the node's LP optimum may exceed 30.
Nothing: any LP value below 30 justifies pruning.
The point should become the new incumbent instead.
The node must instead be pruned for infeasibility.

questions.question: For: maximize $3x_1+2x_2$ subject to $2x_1+2x_2\le9.5$, $x_1\le3.5$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$ integer, the incumbent value is 11, and an open node has fractional LP optimum $(1.75,3)$ with value 11.25. Can the node be discarded without losing any integer solution better than the incumbent?
options: No: its bound 11.25 exceeds the incumbent 11.
No: its optimum is fractional.
Yes: its integer values are at most 11.
Yes: its optimum rounds to $(2,3)$.

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a minimization integer program the incumbent cost is 57. Four new nodes are processed in the order A, B, C, D: A has an infeasible LP, B an integral LP optimum costing 55, C a fractional optimum costing 56.2, and D a fractional optimum costing 54.5. Which nodes still need branching?
options: C and D
Node D only
B, C and D
None of them
